A_over_read.contradictory: an identical tail-4 aligned tensor was read in 5J and 5K without a fault
A_over_read.missing: the instruction and kernel, and whether the faulting read is the one at the page end
A_over_read.supporting: three faults page-exact with a 4-byte tail at a 2 MiB aligned end; no fault when the buffer had slack

B_kernel_or_transpose.contradictory: the asymmetry is inferred from dispatch counts the records cannot fully explain, and in faulting runs the same tensor is read by both formulations
B_kernel_or_transpose.smallest_discriminating_experiment: provenance that names the consumer of the faulting read
B_kernel_or_transpose.supporting: only the runs with a C 256xM OP_N read of the tail-4 tensor faulted; 3 for 3 versus 0 for 2

C_reuse_or_lifetime.contradictory: the tensor is live in the dispatch record at the read, and no double free or use-after-free has been observed
C_reuse_or_lifetime.supporting: the 5N pointer was reused and a stale record for the same address exists; the fault surfaces one iteration later

D_other_kernel.contradictory: the 4-byte tail coincidence recurred in three independent runs at three addresses, each time with an (M,682) operand
D_other_kernel.smallest_discriminating_experiment: a run that removes the tail-4 operand while leaving everything else equal
D_other_kernel.supporting: asynchronous reporting one iteration later; in 5N a second page-exact candidate existed at the same page, an 8 MB stock activation ending exactly on it

instrumentation_design.layer_1: torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history: allocator events with Python stacks, C++ level, no operator interception; dump from the exception handler after a catchable fault
instrumentation_design.layer_2: TorchFunctionMode restricted to BF16 outputs of exactly 4,194,300 bytes, recording producer tag and consumer role
instrumentation_design.reuse_handling: key on (pointer, byte count, lifetime id) and reject joins outside the lifetime; retrospective pointer-only matching is abandoned
instrumentation_design.risk: instrumentation suppressed this fault in PERF-5E, so the first run must be treated as an instrumentation-validity test too

meta.experiment: v3.1-PERF-5O operand provenance and fault reconciliation
meta.kind: CPU-only offline analysis, no GPU execution

next_experiment.arm: unmodified stock reproducer, no padding, with layer 1 and the size-filtered layer 2 enabled, dumping from the exception handler

stop_conditions: ambiguous provenance join for the fault tensor
validity_gates: CPU: instrumentation numerically neutral, whole model bitwise
GPU: at least one tail-4 (M,682) BF16 allocation with a producer stack
GPU: at least one consumer dispatch matching pointer, byte count and lifetime
the fault page matches that tensor's page inside the same lifetime
next_experiment.why: four padding arms produced one clean discrimination and then a contradiction; one provenance run converts the hypotheses from inference to evidence

reconciliation.common_geometry: BF16 GEMM operand, 4,194,300 bytes = (3075,682), 2 MiB aligned, page_dist 4, grid_2mib_dist 4
reconciliation.inferred: the tensor is one of three (M,682) BF16 tensors that can be a GEMM operand; the descriptor pair is produced by three different producer/consumer combinations with identical fields
observed: fault page lies in no padded storage in 5I, 5L and 5N
unknown: no allocation record exists for the 5N fault pointer, so it was allocated by ATen, not by the harness
that pointer falls inside a storage the harness recorded earlier for a (3068,682) front-padded product at 0x7f505affb800, so pointer-only matching would wrongly name that product
the clean runs show only the C 256x682 OP_T read, the faulting runs show both shapes; whether that is a role asymmetry or a dispatch artefact is unresolved
no artifact records the allocating operator or a tensor lifetime

candidates_by_arm.reason: the product is provably padded in 5N (its single (3075,682) record is at 0x7f4f9ef50000) and in 5J/5K
